import java.util.*;
import java.io.*;

public class _1599_C {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        BufferedReader in = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));
        PrintWriter out = new PrintWriter(System.out);
        String[] tokens = in.readLine().split("\\s+");
        int n = Integer.parseInt(tokens[0]);
        double p = Double.parseDouble(tokens[1]);
        
        // Handle edge case where p is 0
        if (p == 0) {
            out.println(0);
            in.close();
            out.close();
            return;
        }
        
        int total = comb3(n);
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            double prob = 0.0;
            
            // Case 1: Johnny studies i maps
            // The system selects 3 maps from n total maps
            
            // Case 1: All 3 selected maps are among Johnny's studied maps (i maps)
            // Johnny can discard any of the 3, opponents discard randomly
            // If all 3 are studied, game will be on studied map regardless of discards
            prob += (double) comb3(i) / total;
            
            // Case 2: Exactly 2 of the 3 selected maps are among Johnny's studied maps
            // Johnny will discard the un-studied one, opponents discard randomly
            // If both opponents discard the same map (either one of the studied ones), 
            // then the remaining map is studied. If they discard different maps,
            // the system picks randomly between the remaining two (one studied, one not)
            // Probability that game is on studied map = 1/2
            prob += (double) (comb2(i) * (n - i)) / total * 0.5;
            
            // Case 3: Exactly 1 of the 3 selected maps is among Johnny's studied maps
            // Johnny will discard the studied one (to avoid playing on unknown map)
            // Opponents discard randomly among 3 maps
            // For game to be on studied map, both opponents must discard the same un-studied map
            // There are (n-i) un-studied maps, each opponent picks one to discard uniformly at random
            // Probability both discard same specific un-studied map = 1/3 * 1/3 = 1/9
            // But we need probability that both discard the same map (any of the (n-i) un-studied)
            // Actually, each opponent independently picks one of 3 maps to discard uniformly
            // For the studied map to be played, both opponents must discard the same un-studied map
            // There are 3 maps: 1 studied (S), 2 un-studied (U1, U2)
            // Johnny discards S. Opponents each pick one of {S, U1, U2} to discard
            // For S to be selected, both opponents must discard the same un-studied map
            // If both discard U1, then remaining maps are S and U2, system picks randomly -> 1/2 chance for S
            // If both discard U2, then remaining maps are S and U1, system picks randomly -> 1/2 chance for S
            // If one discards U1 and other discards U2, remaining maps are S and the one not discarded by either
            // Actually, let's reconsider: after Johnny discards S, we have U1 and U2 left
            // Each opponent picks one of the original 3 maps to discard
            // If both opponents discard the same map (whether S, U1, or U2):
            //   - If both discard S: remaining maps are U1, U2 -> game not on studied map
            //   - If both discard U1: remaining maps are S, U2 -> 1/2 chance for S
            //   - If both discard U2: remaining maps are S, U1 -> 1/2 chance for S
            // If opponents discard different maps:
            //   - One discards U1, other discards U2: remaining map is S -> game on studied map
            //   - One discards S, other discards U1: remaining maps are U2 -> not studied
            //   - One discards S, other discards U2: remaining maps are U1 -> not studied
            // So probability = P(both discard same un-studied)*1/2 + P(discard different un-studied)*1
            // P(both discard U1) = 1/3 * 1/3 = 1/9
            // P(both discard U2) = 1/3 * 1/3 = 1/9
            // P(one discards U1, other U2) = 2 * 1/3 * 1/3 = 2/9
            // Total = (1/9 + 1/9) * 1/2 + 2/9 = 2/9 * 1/2 + 2/9 = 1/9 + 2/9 = 3/9 = 1/3
            
            // Actually, let me recalculate more carefully:
            // Maps: S (studied), U1, U2 (un-studied)
            // Johnny discards S
            // Opponent 1 picks one of {S, U1, U2} uniformly
            // Opponent 2 picks one of {S, U1, U2} uniformly
            // Remaining maps = original 3 minus {S, discard1, discard2} (removing duplicates)
            // If discard1 == discard2 == S: remaining = {U1, U2} -> 0 chance for S
            // If discard1 == discard2 == U1: remaining = {S, U2} -> 1/2 chance for S
            // If discard1 == discard2 == U2: remaining = {S, U1} -> 1/2 chance for S
            // If discard1 == S, discard2 == U1: remaining = {U2} -> 0 chance
            // If discard1 == S, discard2 == U2: remaining = {U1} -> 0 chance
            // If discard1 == U1, discard2 == S: remaining = {U2} -> 0 chance
            // If discard1 == U2, discard2 == S: remaining = {U1} -> 0 chance
            // If discard1 == U1, discard2 == U2: remaining = {S} -> 1 chance
            // If discard1 == U2, discard2 == U1: remaining = {S} -> 1 chance
            // 
            // Probabilities:
            // P(both S) = 1/9, contribution = 0
            // P(both U1) = 1/9, contribution = 1/2 * 1/9 = 1/18
            // P(both U2) = 1/9, contribution = 1/2 * 1/9 = 1/18
            // P(S,U1) = 1/9, contribution = 0
            // P(S,U2) = 1/9, contribution = 0
            // P(U1,S) = 1/9, contribution = 0
            // P(U2,S) = 1/9, contribution = 0
            // P(U1,U2) = 1/9, contribution = 1 * 1/9 = 1/9
            // P(U2,U1) = 1/9, contribution = 1 * 1/9 = 1/9
            // Total = 1/18 + 1/18 + 1/9 + 1/9 = 2/18 + 2/9 = 1/9 + 2/9 = 3/9 = 1/3
            
            prob += (double) (i * comb2(n - i)) / total * (1.0/3.0);
            
            // Case 4: 0 of the 3 selected maps are among Johnny's studied maps
            // Probability = 0 since none are studied
            // This case contributes 0
            
            if (prob >= p) {
                out.println(i);
                break;
            }
        }
        in.close();
        out.close();
    }
    
    private static int comb2(int x) {
        return x < 2 ? 0 : x * (x - 1) / 2;
    }
    
    private static int comb3(int x) {
        return x < 3 ? 0 : x * (x - 1) * (x - 2) / 6;
    }
}
